findings.comment: Building elevation sheets with surveyed overhead conductor locations and clearance dimensions are required to demonstrate that buildings maintain minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from the outside conductor of overhead electric lines. No such documentation is present on the site plan.
applicableAreas: Buildings 1-8, particularly Building 1 and Building 8 (closest to overhead electric lines on western and southern boundaries)
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) confirms overhead electric utility lines (O.H.U.L.) with utility poles exist along Valley View Road (western boundary) and southern property boundary. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows buildings 1-8 with Building 1 dimensioned at 26.1' and Building 8 at 26.6' from the western property line. Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) references existing OHE lines. However, NO building elevation sheets are provided in the 39-sheet set. NO dimension annotations show horizontal clearances from buildings to the outside conductor of overhead lines. NO surveyed conductor elevations are shown on any drawings.
findings.reasoning: While buildings are set back approximately 26+ feet from the property line, the requirement is to maintain a 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from the OUTSIDE CONDUCTOR of overhead electric conductors. Without surveyed conductor elevation data, clearance dimensions from the outside conductor to building faces, and no building elevation drawings showing the vertical relationship, it is impossible to verify that the minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance is maintained. The code requires clearance measured from the outside conductor (which may be offset several feet from the pole center on multi-conductor installations), not from the pole or property line. Applicant has acknowledged responsibility for maintaining clearances (Sheet 3, Block 8), but has not provided the necessary documentation to demonstrate compliance.

findings.comment: No building elevation sheets or dimension callouts showing 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from outside conductor to Buildings 7 and 8. Provide registered surveyor elevation data and clearance dimension annotations.
applicableAreas: Buildings 7 and 8 on southern boundary adjacent to OHE line
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) depicts an overhead electric line (OHE) routing along and crossing the site. Sheet 9 (Proposed Site Plan) shows this OHE line running along the southern boundary of the property. Buildings 7 and 8 are positioned closest to this southern boundary. However, no clearance dimension lines or annotations are provided on either the site plan or any building elevation sheets showing the horizontal distance from the buildings' exterior walls or projections to the OHE conductor. No profile/section views are provided showing vertical clearances. The plans do not identify whether the OHE line is a primary, secondary, or neutral conductor, nor is there a surveyed elevation of the conductor provided. No dimension callouts originate from the conductor location itself—the critical measurement baseline required by code.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires buildings to maintain minimum 7.5 feet horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead electric conductors. This measurement must be from the outside conductor, not from the pole. The applicant has not provided evidence that this clearance is maintained. Without (1) building elevation sheets showing surveyed conductor elevations, (2) dimension annotations from the outside conductor to the building face, or (3) a registered surveyor's proximity survey per UCM § 1.10.3, the reviewer cannot determine whether the requirement is met. The conservative approach is to flag this as unclear pending submittal of required elevation documentation and proximity survey data.

findings.comment: Proposed buildings do not show measured clearance dimensions from the outside conductor of overhead electric lines. All buildings with potential clearance concerns require clearance dimension annotations on site plan and building elevation sheets, measured from the outside (outermost) conductor, demonstrating minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance is maintained per UCM § 1.10.3.
applicableAreas: Buildings and permanent structures throughout the site
findings.observation: The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) clearly shows overhead utility lines (O.H.U.L.) running along Valley View Road (western boundary) and the northern property boundary, with utility poles marked. The proposed site plan (Sheet 9) shows eight multi-story residential buildings (ranging from 33'-5" to 36'-1" in height) positioned on the site. The overhead electric utility line is labeled '----OHE----' on the site plan running along the Valley View Road frontage (southern boundary). However, NO clearance dimensions are annotated anywhere on Sheet 9 showing the horizontal distance from the outside conductor of the overhead line to any building face or structure. No building elevation sheets with surveyed conductor locations and clearance dimensions were found in the submitted plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires buildings to maintain a minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead primary, neutral, and secondary conductors. The regulation defines this as a vertical plane extending infinitely upward from a point 7.5 feet from the conductor. The site plan shows buildings within reasonable proximity to the overhead lines along Valley View Road, but the applicant has provided no dimensional evidence that the 7.5-foot minimum horizontal clearance is maintained. The absence of clearance annotations and dimensions constitutes a failure to demonstrate compliance. Per the grouping documentation, clearance dimensions must be labeled on plans with dimension lines originating from the actual outside conductor location (not pole centerline).

findings.comment: Building elevation sheets prepared by the architect/engineer are required, showing surveyed overhead conductor elevations with clearance dimension annotations from the conductor to building faces, roofs, parapets, and all projections, for all buildings within potential clearance distance of overhead electric facilities.
applicableAreas: All buildings proposed within potential clearance distance of overhead electric facilities
findings.observation: The 39-sheet site plan set does not include any building elevation sheets. Sheet 9 shows building footprints and FFEs but is a plan view only. The README index lists sheets 1-39 with the following titles: Sheets 1-11 are general plans; Sheets 12-20 are utility and drainage plans; Sheets 21-39 are details and landscape plans. NO sheets titled 'Building Elevations,' 'Building Elevation Sheets,' or similar are listed. Consequently, surveyed overhead conductor elevations and clearance dimension annotations are not present on any elevation sheets.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 explicitly requires surveyed elevations and locations of overhead conductors to be included on building elevation sheets to demonstrate required clearances are met. The absence of building elevation sheets constitutes a failure to provide the required documentation. The code requirement is specific: 'Surveyed elevations and locations of overhead conductors not included on building elevation sheets to demonstrate required clearances are met' is identified as a deficiency.

findings.comment: Building elevation sheets with surveyed overhead conductor elevations are missing. Provide building elevation drawings showing surveyed conductor locations and clearance dimensions to all building faces and projections.
applicableAreas: Buildings 7 and 8 adjacent to southern OHE line; entire site with overhead facilities
findings.observation: No building elevation sheets are included in the 39-sheet site plan set. The README index lists sheets 1-39 as site/civil engineering and landscape drawings, with no architectural elevation sheets shown. Existing overhead electric lines are depicted on Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions) and Sheet 9 (Proposed Site Plan), but no surveyed conductor elevation data is provided on any sheet. No registered surveyor's mid-span clearance measurements are documented. The electrical survey required by Austin Energy Design per UCM § 1.10.3 does not appear to have been submitted.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 explicitly requires that surveyed elevations and locations of overhead conductors be included on building elevation sheets to demonstrate required clearances are met. The applicant has not submitted any building elevation sheets. This is a mandatory documentation requirement for any site with buildings within clearance distance of overhead electric facilities. The absence of this required documentation constitutes a deficiency regardless of actual clearances that might exist on the ground.

findings.comment: Building elevation sheets do not show surveyed elevations of existing overhead electric conductors. Sealed building elevation exhibits are required for all buildings with potential proximity to overhead lines, showing the surveyed elevation of the outside conductor and dimensioned clearances from the conductor to building faces and projections.
applicableAreas: Building elevation documentation
findings.observation: The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) documents existing overhead utility lines running along the property boundary and service drop. The proposed buildings range from 33'-4.75" to 36'-1" in height. A complete set of building elevation sheets showing the surveyed elevation of the existing overhead conductors is not present in the submitted site plan set. While general notes on Sheet 3 reference benchmarks (B.M. #1 at 678.52' and B.M. #2 at 681.08' NAVD 88), these are general site control points, not surveyed overhead conductor elevations. No building elevation exhibits were found that show the actual conductor elevation overlaid with the building profile to verify vertical clearances.
findings.reasoning: Per the grouping's Documentation Requirements section, 'Profile plans: Engineered, sealed profile drawings showing vertical relationships between overhead conductors and building features, including overhangs, balconies, and canopies, with dimensioned clearances' are required. The grouping cites UCM § 1.10.3 as requiring permanent clearances and explicitly states that clearance verification requires 'surveyed elevations and locations of overhead conductors included on building elevation sheets.' Without surveyed conductor elevation data on building elevation sheets, the applicant cannot demonstrate that the 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance or other required clearances are met.

findings.comment: Provide section view exhibits (with title callouts such as Section A-A, B-B) on site plan or separate detail sheets showing dimension lines from the surveyed outside conductor location to the outermost edges of each building and all building projections, clearly labeling clearances in feet and inches.
applicableAreas: Buildings 1-8 and retaining walls adjacent to overhead electric lines
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows buildings in plan view only with no section line callouts (A-A, B-B, etc.) that would reference section views showing clearances. Sheet 22 shows standard construction details for curbs, sidewalks, and driveways but contains no section views specifically showing clearances from outer electric conductor to building edges. Sheets 38-39 show wall construction details and sections but not clearance dimensions from overhead conductors to wall faces. Examined sheets do not include section or plan view exhibits with dimension lines originating at the outer electric conductor and extending to building edges or wall faces.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires 'Section and plan view exhibits [that] show dimensions from outer electric conductor to outermost edge of buildings and building projections for clearance verification.' This is a specific documentation requirement. The absence of any section views with dimension lines from the outer conductor to building edges or wall faces constitutes non-compliance. The requirement applies when buildings or structures are proposed within potential clearance distance, which is the case here.

findings.comment: No section/profile exhibits provided showing clearance dimensions from outer conductor to buildings and site features. Provide detailed section and plan views with dimension callouts from outside conductor to building edges and site improvements.
applicableAreas: Buildings 7 and 8; parking areas; all structures within clearance distance of OHE line
findings.observation: No section or profile view exhibits are provided showing dimensions from the outer electric conductor to the outermost edge of buildings and site improvements. Sheet 9 (Proposed Site Plan) shows the OHE line and buildings in plan view only, without any profile views. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows contours and building FFEs but does not show overhead conductor elevation or clearance dimensions. No enlarged plan details with cross-section views have been submitted showing the relationship between conductors and building edges, parking surfaces, or driveways.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires dimension lines from the outer conductor to outermost building edges in plan and section views to verify clearance compliance. These dimension annotations are mandatory and must originate from the actual conductor location, not from the pole. The complete absence of section and profile exhibits with clearance dimensions is a deficiency. The applicant must provide these required exhibits.

findings.comment: Section and plan view exhibits do not show dimensions from the outside electric conductor to the outermost edges of proposed buildings, building projections, and other site features. Enlarged plan details and section views are required showing dimension lines originating from the outside conductor and extending to all building faces and structures within potential clearance distance, demonstrating compliance with the 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance requirement.
applicableAreas: Site plan sections and elevation views
findings.observation: The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) clearly identifies overhead utility lines with the notation 'O.H.U.L.' running along Valley View Road and the northern property boundary. The proposed site plan (Sheet 9) and landscape plan (Sheet 31) both show overhead electric lines (labeled 'OHE' or '----OHE----') but NO dimension lines or clearance annotations extending from the outside conductor to the outer edges of any buildings, projections, site features, or structures. No section views or profile exhibits were found showing the cross-section relationship between the overhead conductor and site features. The landscape plan shows trees proposed near the OHE line but with no distance callouts or species specifications.
findings.reasoning: The grouping explicitly states: 'Common Violation Patterns: Clearances measured from pole instead of conductor... Dimension annotations read "10'-0" from pole" instead of "15'-0" from outside conductor"' and 'Missing profile plans: Site plan shows building and overhead lines in plan view only, no elevation/section view; no surveyed mid-span clearance data; cannot verify vertical clearances meet requirements.' UCM § 1.10.3 requires permanent clearances, which must be demonstrated through dimension callouts showing measurement from the outside (outermost) conductor to the building edge. The complete absence of these dimensions constitutes a deficiency.

findings.comment: Provide grading profile sections for proposed driveways showing surveyed overhead conductor elevations at the low point and dimension annotations verifying minimum 16-foot or 18-foot vertical clearance (depending on truck traffic designation) from the lowest point of all overhead conductors and attached equipment to the finished driveway surface.
applicableAreas: Proposed driveways crossing or passing under or adjacent to overhead electric facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows driveways marked 'Construct Type II Driveway' and 'Construct Type III Driveway' on the western and internal portions of the site. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows existing and proposed contours with driveway grades and spot elevations, but contains NO profile sections showing the vertical clearance from lowest point of overhead conductors (including any attached telecommunications lines) to the driveway surface. Sheet 22 shows standard driveway construction details (thickness, reinforcement, grades) but NO sections showing vertical clearance to overhead lines. The FFE elevations of buildings are provided (ranging from 683' to 687.5' NAVD 88), but overhead conductor elevations are not given.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.6.2 requires driveways to maintain minimum 16-foot vertical clearance (for parking without truck traffic) or 18-foot vertical clearance (for areas with truck traffic) from the lowest point of overhead electric facilities including telecommunications attachments. This requires (1) surveyed conductor height data, (2) profile or section views showing clearance calculations, and (3) mid-span clearance verification if the clearance appears marginal. None of these are provided. Applicant has not verified mid-span clearances with registered surveyor data, and no vertical clearance dimensions are shown on grading or profile sheets.

findings.comment: No documented vertical clearance from finished driveway grades to overhead electric line. Provide grading plan section views with finished elevations at OHE line crossing and surveyed conductor height; specify truck traffic classification.
applicableAreas: Internal driveways and parking areas on southern portion of site where OHE line is routed
findings.observation: Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows finished floor elevations and site contours but does not provide finished driveway grade elevations at specific locations relative to the OHE line shown on Sheet 9. No section views are provided showing the vertical relationship between the lowest point of the overhead electric line and the finished grade of parking/drive areas. Truck traffic classification (which determines 16-foot vs. 18-foot clearance requirement) is not specified on the plans. No mid-span clearance measurements from a registered surveyor are provided.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.6.2 requires minimum 16-foot vertical clearance for parking without truck traffic, or 18-foot with truck traffic, from the lowest point of overhead electric facilities (including service drops and telecommunications attachments). Without (1) documented finished grade elevations at driveway locations, (2) surveyed overhead line heights, and (3) specification of truck traffic usage, compliance cannot be verified. The applicant must provide site/utility profile views with documented vertical clearances.

findings.comment: The proposed driveway crosses the existing overhead electric line at Valley View Road. No section views, surveyed mid-span clearance measurements, or vertical clearance dimension annotations are provided to demonstrate the minimum 16-foot (or 18-foot for truck traffic areas) vertical clearance from the lowest point of the overhead line to the finished driveway grade. A registered surveyor's survey showing mid-span clearance is required, with results documented on section views and profile sheets.
applicableAreas: Proposed driveway intersection with overhead utility line at Valley View Road frontage
findings.observation: The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows an overhead utility line labeled 'O.H.U.L.' running along Valley View Road (western boundary). The proposed site plan (Sheet 9) shows a proposed driveway at the bottom left (Valley View Road frontage) area. Per the vision analysis of Sheet 9, the proposed driveway 'crosses directly under the horizontal ----OHE---- line' along Valley View Road. The grading plan (Sheet 11) shows the finished floor elevations and site grades but does not annotate the vertical clearance dimensions at the driveway location where the overhead line crosses. No registered surveyor data showing mid-span clearance measurements is provided. The roadway grade elevations are not dimensioned relative to the overhead line height.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.6.2 specifies: 'Driveway and parking without truck traffic: 16 feet minimum vertical clearance; Roads, streets, alleys, and areas with truck traffic: 18 feet minimum vertical clearance from lowest point of overhead electric facilities including telecommunications attachments.' The grouping documentation notes this is a 'Common Violation Pattern: Inadequate service-drop clearances: Driveway grade shown within 15-16 feet of overhead service drop without mid-span clearance verification; service drop sag at maximum load/temperature may contact vehicles.' Since the proposed driveway crosses under the overhead line, vertical clearance must be verified through surveyed mid-span clearance data showing the lowest point of the conductor at maximum sag. The absence of this documentation constitutes a failure to demonstrate compliance.

findings.comment: Clearance verification exhibits are not provided, not engineered and sealed, or not included in the permitted plan set. No exhibits demonstrating compliance with both the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance AND 15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution conductors (measured from outer conductor per AEDC § 1.10.3) are visible on the submitted site plan. Please provide engineered and sealed clearance verification exhibits showing both required clearance envelopes around all proposed structures and existing electric facilities.
applicableAreas: Entire site where proposed structures may be within clearance zones of existing electric facilities
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) and Sheet 9 (Site Plan). Both sheets show existing overhead electric line (OHE) labeled along southern property boundary near street. Sheet 21 shows proposed transformer pad and underground electric lines. However, NO clearance verification exhibits were found. The sheets show facility locations but do NOT include engineered exhibits demonstrating compliance with AEDC § 1.10.3 clearance standards. Neither sheet shows calculated clearance zones, clearance dimensions measured from outer conductors, or exhibits demonstrating that the dual clearance envelope requirements (7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance AND 15-foot radius clearance) are satisfied. No profile or cross-section views with clearance dimensions are provided.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(2) and § 1.10.3 require clearance verification exhibits when proposed structures are located within required clearance zones of existing electric facilities. The grouping regulatory overview emphasizes that BOTH clearance envelopes must be satisfied simultaneously and that clearances must be measured from the outer conductor, not pole centerline. Without engineered exhibits demonstrating these calculations, the applicant has not provided evidence of compliance. The burden of proof is on the applicant to demonstrate code compliance through specific exhibits; showing facility locations alone is insufficient.

findings.comment: Clearance verification exhibits not provided. Plans must include engineered and sealed exhibits demonstrating both 7'-6" minimum horizontal sky-to-ground clearance AND 15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution conductors (measured from outer conductor, not pole centerline). Exhibits must be drawn to scale and included in permitted plan set.
applicableAreas: Electric facility design - entire site
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9, 21, and 3 for clearance verification exhibits. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electrical infrastructure layout with transformers, pull boxes, and underground lines, but no clearance verification exhibits are present. No engineered drawings demonstrating both 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and 15-foot radius clearance envelopes from conductors are provided. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed electrical elements are shown and labeled with adequate scale (1" = 20'), but no clearance exhibits exist. Master Comment Report Section 02 identifies Austin Energy Design Requirements including UCM § 1.10.3 (Permanent Clearances from AE Overhead Lines) as applicable, confirming clearance compliance must be demonstrated.
findings.reasoning: The grouping specifies clearance exhibits must demonstrate code compliance showing both 7'-6" horizontal AND 15-foot radius clearance envelopes. The vision analysis confirmed no such exhibits are present. The requirement applies because proposed structures are located in areas potentially affecting existing utility easements and overhead electric lines. Austin Energy's Master Comment Report lists clearance standards as preliminary design requirements, making exhibits mandatory for land development review approval.

findings.comment: No clearance verification exhibits provided demonstrating compliance with both the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and 15-foot radius cylindrical clearance requirements from overhead distribution conductors as required by AEDC § 1.10.3. Engineered and sealed clearance exhibits must be included in the permitted plan set.
applicableAreas: Site-wide clearance zones around existing electric facilities
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) and Sheet 9 (Site Plan) to determine if clearance verification exhibits are provided. Sheet 21 shows underground electric lines, transformers, pull boxes, and meters with building footprints and FFEs labeled. Sheet 9 shows electric facility locations with property lines and easement boundaries. No dedicated clearance verification exhibits found on any sheet examined. No sheet displays both required clearance envelopes: the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance extending infinitely upward from 7.5 feet horizontal distance from conductors, AND the 15-foot radius cylindrical clearance extending infinitely downward from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. No engineered and sealed clearance exhibit sheets appear in the 39-sheet plan set.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires clearance verification exhibits to be 'engineered and scaled' and 'included in the permitted plan set' when proposed structures are located within required clearance zones. AEDC § 1.16.0(2) mandates this documentation. While the electrical design plan shows proposed structures and electric facility locations, it does not provide a dedicated exhibit demonstrating compliance with both the 7'-6" horizontal AND 15-foot radius clearance requirements. The absence of clearance verification exhibits means the applicant cannot demonstrate code compliance with these dual clearance envelopes, which the grouping Regulatory Overview specifies must BOTH be satisfied simultaneously—satisfying one does not satisfy the other.

findings.comment: Profile or cross-section drawings are not provided demonstrating clearances between proposed structures (including overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) and existing electric facilities/easements. Please provide engineered profile drawings showing all building elements with dimensions and clearances measured to the outer conductors of overhead electric lines.
applicableAreas: All areas where proposed structures may be within clearance zones of existing electric facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 21 is a plan-view drawing only. No profile drawings, cross-section drawings, or elevation views showing vertical clearances have been found. While Sheet 21 shows basic building footprints with Finished Floor Elevations (FFE) for each building, no details show building element dimensions such as overhangs, balconies, awnings, or canopies with their heights and horizontal extents relative to existing or proposed electric facilities. No profile views showing clearances between structures and electric facilities/easements are provided.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.10.3 requires profile or cross-section drawings demonstrating clearances when structures (including overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) are located within required clearance zones. The grouping regulatory overview explicitly states that 'Profile plans must be engineered, sealed, and drawn to scale showing all building elements (including overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) with dimensioned clearances.' The applicant has not provided these critical documents, making it impossible to verify clearance compliance in the vertical plane.

findings.comment: Profile or cross-section drawings not provided demonstrating clearances between proposed structures (including overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) and existing electric facilities. Submit building elevations and profile drawings showing dimensioned clearances measured from outer conductors for all building elements that could encroach on clearance zones.
applicableAreas: Building structures - all 8 buildings
findings.observation: Searched document set for building elevations, profile drawings, and cross-section exhibits showing clearances. No building elevation sheets exist in the primary site plan (39 sheets total). Sheet 9 shows building footprints and heights in tables (ranging from 33'-4.75" to 36'-1"), but no elevations depicting building elements. No cross-section drawings showing vertical clearances between proposed structures and existing electric facilities are present.
findings.reasoning: The grouping defines this item as applicable only when proposed structures are within required clearance zones. Sheet 9 and Sheet 31 vision confirmed the presence of overhead electric facilities on the site (5' Electric Easement, 15' Elec. & Tele. Easement, and OHE line on southern boundary). Building elevations or profile drawings are required to show clearances but are completely absent. Without these drawings, clearances cannot be verified as required by AEDC § 1.10.3.

findings.comment: Profile or cross-section drawings not provided demonstrating clearances between proposed building elements (including overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) and existing electric facilities. Engineered profiles drawn to scale and sealed must show vertical clearances and building element dimensions.
applicableAreas: All building elevations where overhangs, balconies, awnings, or canopies exist
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) for profile/cross-section drawings showing clearances. Found only plan view with building footprints and FFEs; no profiles shown on this sheet. Examined Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) which contains detailed water utility profiles at 1"=20' horizontal and 1"=2' vertical scale. However, these profiles show ONLY water utility lines and do not include electric utility lines or building elements (walls, overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) needed to verify clearances from existing electric facilities. No building elevation sheets provided in the plan set that would show heights and element dimensions of proposed structures. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed: 'Building heights are NOT shown on this plan view. There are no explicitly delineated or labeled building overhangs, balconies, or canopies that might affect vertical clearances.'
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.10.3 and the grouping 'Documents to Review' section specifically require 'Profile Drawings / Cross-section Exhibits' showing 'clearances between proposed structures and existing electric facilities/easements' with 'all building elements (including overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies)' and 'dimensioned clearances.' While utility profiles exist on Sheet 20, they do not include electric utilities or building elements. The electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows only plan view without profiles or building element details. This deficiency prevents verification of compliance with the 7'-6" minimum clearance requirement measured from outer conductors as specified in the measurement methodology.

findings.comment: Clearance dimensions and heights are not specified for building elements, or clearances are measured from pole centerline instead of outer conductor. Please provide dimensioned clearance details on profile drawings showing measurement points from the outer conductor of the overhead electric line, with dimensions to all building elements (overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies).
applicableAreas: All areas with proposed structures within clearance zones of electric facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows building footprints with FFE (Finished Floor Elevations) but no detailed dimensions for building elements (overhangs, balconies, awnings). The sheet shows generic labels for 'Electrical Transformer Pad', 'Electrical Pull Box', and 'Electrical Meters' but these labels lack any dimensional information. No callouts or dimension lines show clearances measured from outer conductors. The existing overhead electric line (OHE) location is noted but with no specific conductor height or clearance calculations. All dimensions and heights necessary for clearance verification from the outer conductor (not pole centerline) are absent.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.10.3 requires that clearance dimensions and heights be specified for all building elements where required for clearance verification. The grouping regulatory overview states: 'Measure from outer conductor (the actual wire), NOT from pole centerline or pole structure. For three-phase overhead lines, measure from the outermost conductor farthest from the pole. Horizontal clearances are measured as horizontal distance only (not diagonal).' The submitted plans show generic facility locations without the specific dimensional callouts required to verify compliance with these measurement standards. This deficiency prevents verifiable clearance review.

findings.comment: Clearance dimensions and heights not specified for building elements. Provide detailed building elevations and profile plans with dimensioned clearances for all roof overhangs, balconies, awnings, and canopies, measured from outer conductor locations showing minimum distances of 7'-6" horizontal and 15-foot radial clearance from overhead distribution conductors.
applicableAreas: Building elevations and profile plans - all structures
findings.observation: Examined all site plan sheets for clearance dimensions and building element heights. Sheet 9 contains a Building Height Table showing overall structure heights, but no dimensions for building elements (roof overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) are provided. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed building FFE values are shown but no dimensional information about projecting elements. No building elevations exist. Clearance dimensions are completely absent from all drawings.
findings.reasoning: This deficiency applies because buildings on the site are in proximity to existing electric easements (Sheet 9 vision confirmed 5' and 15' Electric Easements). Without building elevations showing dimensions of overhangs, balconies, and canopies, and without clearance dimensions measured from outer conductor locations, compliance cannot be demonstrated. The absence of these dimensions represents a critical documentation gap.

findings.comment: Building element heights, clearance dimensions, and outer conductor measurement points not specified on electrical plans or profiles. All clearances must be dimensioned and measured from the outer conductor (actual wire) location, not from pole centerline.
applicableAreas: All building elements and electric facility locations
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows building footprints with Finished Floor Elevations (FFEs) labeled for all 8 buildings (e.g., Bldg. 1 FFE=687.50, Bldg. 5 FFE=683.0). However, no building heights are shown. No dimensions specify clearance distances from electric facilities to building elements. Vision analysis confirmed: 'The labels provide only generic identification. There is NO specific information provided on this sheet regarding voltage, size, equipment type (e.g., single-phase vs. three-phase), or ownership (e.g., Austin Energy vs. Private) for these facilities.' Transformer, pull box, and meter locations are shown but not dimensioned relative to property lines, building corners, or other reference points. No specification of clearances measured from outer conductor locations.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires 'Clearance dimensions and heights' to be 'specified for building elements' and 'clearances measured from outer conductor locations.' The Regulatory Overview emphasizes: 'Measure from outer conductor (the actual wire), NOT from pole centerline' and 'For three-phase overhead lines, measure from the outermost conductor farthest from the pole.' Sheet 21 contains no such dimensioning. The absence of building height dimensions, clearance measurements, and specification of measurement points from outer conductors means the plans do not demonstrate compliance with the clearance measurement methodology required by code.

findings.comment: Clearance verification exhibits show only one clearance envelope (or neither envelope) instead of both envelopes required by code. Please provide clearance verification exhibits demonstrating BOTH the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance AND the 15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution conductors, clearly showing both envelopes on the same exhibit(s).
applicableAreas: Entire site where overhead distribution primary or neutral conductors are present
findings.observation: No clearance verification exhibits of any kind were found on Sheets 9 or 21. The site plan shows an existing overhead electric line (OHE) labeled along the southern property boundary. However, there are NO exhibits demonstrating either the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance envelope OR the 15-foot radius clearance envelope required by code. Neither envelope is depicted, labeled, or calculated on any submitted sheet.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.10.3 establishes two distinct, concurrent clearance requirements: (1) 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and (2) 15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. The grouping regulatory overview emphasizes: 'These are separate envelopes with different geometric properties. Both must be met; satisfying one does not satisfy the other. These requirements are in addition to NESC Section 234 baseline requirements, not substitutes for them.' The applicant has provided neither envelope on the submitted plans, failing to demonstrate compliance with this critical dual-requirement standard.

findings.comment: Clearance verification exhibits do not show both required clearance envelopes. Provide engineered exhibits demonstrating BOTH: (1) 7'-6" minimum horizontal sky-to-ground clearance extending infinitely upward from ground level at 7.5 feet horizontal distance from outer conductors, AND (2) 15-foot radius cylindrical clearance extending infinitely in all directions from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. Both must be shown simultaneously.
applicableAreas: Overhead distribution conductor clearance zones
findings.observation: Searched all sheets for clearance verification exhibits. No exhibits found showing either the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance or the 15-foot radius clearance envelopes. Sheet 9 vision confirmed overhead electric lines are shown along boundaries, and Sheet 31 vision confirmed overhead electric line shown on southern boundary. However, no clearance envelope diagrams exist on any sheet.
findings.reasoning: The presence of overhead distribution facilities confirmed by site vision analysis makes clearance verification mandatory. The grouping explicitly states Austin Energy requires BOTH clearance envelopes be satisfied simultaneously - these are separate envelopes with different geometric properties (7'-6" horizontal plane and 15-foot cylindrical radius). The complete absence of any clearance verification exhibits showing both envelopes means neither can be evaluated. This is distinct from EL-11.1 in that this specifically addresses the dual envelope requirement.

findings.comment: Clearance verification exhibits do not depict both required clearance envelopes: the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance extending infinitely upward from 7.5 feet horizontal distance from conductors, AND the 15-foot radius cylindrical clearance extending downward from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. Both envelopes must be shown simultaneously on all required sheets.
applicableAreas: Overhead distribution electrical facilities shown on electrical and landscape plans
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 21, 9, and 31 for clearance verification exhibits. No clearance verification exhibits found on any sheet. Sheets 9 and 21 show underground electric lines (-E- notation) and some overhead electric lines (-OHE- notation) but provide NO clearance envelope diagrams. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows one overhead electric line at bottom edge labeled '-OHE-' but includes no clearance zones, protection buffers, or clearance envelope drawings. The grouping Regulatory Overview states: 'These are separate envelopes with different geometric properties. Both must be met; satisfying one does not satisfy the other. These requirements are IN ADDITION TO NESC Section 234 baseline requirements, not substitutes for them.' No exhibits demonstrate BOTH envelope requirements simultaneously.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.10.3 requires dual clearance envelopes: (1) 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance, and (2) 15-foot radius cylindrical clearance. The grouping emphasizes these are separate geometric envelopes that must BOTH be satisfied. No exhibits on Sheets 9, 21, or 31 display both clearance envelopes. Sheets show overhead lines existing but provide no graphical demonstration of clearance compliance. The absence of exhibits showing both envelopes means the plans do not demonstrate code compliance with the dual clearance requirements.

findings.comment: Provide registered surveyor field survey data documenting: (1) surveyed elevations of overhead electric conductors at mid-span locations above buildings, driveways, and parking areas; (2) calculated vertical clearances from the lowest point of conductors (including attachments) to the highest points of buildings, roof projections, driveways, and parking surfaces, demonstrating compliance with minimum clearance thresholds (7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground for buildings, 16-18 feet for driveways/parking, others as applicable); (3) marked survey points and elevation measurements with registered surveyor certification.
applicableAreas: All proposed driveways, parking areas, buildings, and site features with potential vertical clearance concerns from overhead electric lines
findings.observation: Overhead electric lines (O.H.U.L.) are shown on existing survey (Sheet 4) and electrical plan (Sheet 21) but NO surveyed conductor elevation data is provided anywhere on the 39-sheet site plan set. Buildings have FFEs ranging from 683' to 687.5' (Sheet 9, 11), but overhead conductor heights are not documented. Driveways and parking pads have grading elevations shown (Sheet 11), but no profile sections with surveyed mid-span clearance data verify vertical clearances meet requirements. The vision analysis of Sheet 9 noted that buildings are approximately 26-30 feet horizontally from overhead lines on the western boundary—this distance is close enough that vertical clearance verification (mid-span clearance) should be provided per UCM § 1.10.3 guidance for situations where 'clearance appears marginal or insufficient.' No registered surveyor data confirming mid-span clearance is provided.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires 'survey by registered surveyor showing pole locations and mid-span clearances not provided when existing overhead facilities may not meet minimum vertical clearance requirements.' The grouping guidance states that when vertical clearance 'appears marginal or insufficient based on site plan data,' registered surveyor mid-span clearance data is required. The site plan does not provide surveyed conductor elevations, making it impossible to calculate vertical clearances from building FFEs and driveway grades to conductor height. Furthermore, the presence of structures within approximately 26-30 feet horizontally of overhead lines, combined with the absence of conducted elevator data, suggests that clearance verification is required but not provided. This is a deficiency: applicant has failed to provide surveyor data for mid-span clearances.

findings.comment: No registered surveyor mid-span clearance measurements provided despite buildings and parking areas being positioned adjacent to overhead electric line. Provide licensed surveyor measurements of overhead conductor heights and clearances to all proposed structures and site features.
applicableAreas: Buildings 7 and 8; parking and driveway areas adjacent to southern OHE line
findings.observation: Sheet 4 shows an existing OHE line with utility poles routed across the property. Sheet 9 shows Buildings 7 and 8 and parking/driveway areas positioned immediately adjacent to this overhead line (on southern boundary). Without seeing surveyed conductor elevations or documented clearance measurements, the vertical clearance appears potentially marginal—the minimum required clearances (7.5-foot sky-to-ground, 16-18-foot for driveways, 7.5-foot for parking) cannot be visually confirmed from plan-view drawings alone. No mid-span clearance survey data from a registered surveyor is provided to document actual measured clearances.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires a registered surveyor's mid-span clearance measurements when existing overhead facilities may not meet minimum vertical clearance requirements or when visual determination is insufficient. Given the close proximity of buildings and parking to the OHE line shown on the plans, and the complete absence of vertical clearance documentation, a registered surveyor's measurement is required to verify compliance. The applicant has not provided this required survey work.

findings.comment: No building elevation sheets are provided. Site has existing overhead electric poles and lines adjacent to Valley View Road. Building elevations are required to show the relationship between proposed structures and existing electric poles/lines, and to verify compliance with clearance standards per UCM § 1.10.3 (7.5 ft horizontal, 15 ft radial clearance from overhead distribution lines).
applicableAreas: Locations of existing utility poles and streetlights adjacent to proposed buildings
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) documents existing distribution poles with power lines along Valley View Road (western and southern property boundaries) and shows the overhead utility line (O.H.U.L.) symbols. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the site layout and building locations. However, the site plan set contains no building elevation sheets. The README.md lists 39 sheets in the site plan, primarily focused on site plan, grading, drainage, landscape, details, and utility plans—no architectural building elevation sheets are included. Without building elevations, the three-dimensional relationship between existing poles/lines and proposed buildings cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) explicitly requires that 'Building elevations shall be provided showing proposed structures with streets, streetlights, and electric poles.' This is a mandatory documentation requirement when electric poles or streetlights exist on or adjacent to the site. The applicant has not provided any building elevation sheets. This deficiency directly prevents verification of clearance compliance between proposed structures and existing overhead electric facilities.

findings.comment: Building elevations not provided showing proposed structures with adjacent streets (Valley View Road), streetlights, and electric poles. Provide front and side elevations for all buildings showing the relationship to Valley View Road, existing poles, and overhead/underground facilities per UCM § 1.16.0(2).
applicableAreas: All proposed buildings
Relationship to existing Valley View Road, poles, and streetlights
findings.observation: The site plan submittal (39 sheets total) contains detailed site plans, grading plans, utility plans, and landscape plans, but does NOT include any building elevation sheets. Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows existing site features and property context, but no building elevation views have been identified in the submittal. UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires building elevations showing the relationship between proposed structures and existing public infrastructure including streets, streetlights, and electric poles. The absence of building elevation sheets representing the buildings' relationship to Valley View Road and any adjacent utility poles/streetlights is a clear deficiency in the required documentation.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) explicitly requires building elevations to show the relationship between proposed structures and existing streets, streetlights, and electric poles. These elevation views are essential for demonstrating clearance compliance and understanding site context. The site plan submittal includes plan views and details but lacks the elevation views specifically required by code. This is a documentation requirement that must be satisfied through the addition of building elevation sheets for all buildings, showing their relationship to Valley View Road and any adjacent utility infrastructure.

findings.comment: No building elevation sheets are provided showing the relationship between proposed buildings and electric easements (north, south, and east boundaries). Building elevations are required to verify that proposed structures do not conflict with easement access or clearance requirements.
applicableAreas: Relationship of proposed buildings to electric easements and facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) identifies 5-foot electric and telephone easements on the north and south property boundaries and a 5-foot public utility easement on the east boundary. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the building layout relative to the property boundaries. However, no building elevation sheets are provided that would demonstrate how the proposed buildings relate to these easements or to overhead/underground electric facilities in three dimensions.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires 'Building elevations showing the relationship between buildings and electric easements/facilities' when electric easements or facilities are near proposed buildings. The site has documented electric easements (5-foot width on multiple boundaries), yet the applicant has not provided building elevations to show this relationship. This is a documentation deficiency that prevents verification of easement impacts and clearance compliance.

findings.comment: Building elevations not provided showing relationship between proposed buildings and electric easements on property. Provide building elevation views from the direction of electric easements showing the spatial relationship between structures and easement areas per UCM § 1.16.0(2).
applicableAreas: Relationship between Buildings 1-8 and electric easements on property
findings.observation: The site plan documents show electric easements on the grading plan (Sheet 11) labeled as '5' Electric Easement' and '15' Electric Easement' located along property boundaries. However, there are no building elevation sheets showing the three-dimensional relationship between the proposed buildings and these electric easements. The code requires building elevations to show this relationship. Sheet 9 shows buildings and easement boundaries in plan view, but plan view alone does not adequately demonstrate the spatial relationship required by code. The absence of building elevation sheets means the required relationship documentation is missing.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires building elevations to show the relationship between proposed buildings and electric easements/facilities. This is distinct from plan view representation. Elevations provide a view perpendicular to the lot line and show how buildings sit relative to easement areas, heights above easement grades, and clearances. Without elevation views, this required documentation cannot be verified. Building elevation sheets must be provided to show all buildings' relationships to the electric easements depicted on the property.

findings.comment: No building elevation sheets are provided showing existing electric poles, overhead lines, conductors, cross arms, and property boundaries. Building elevations are required to demonstrate adequate clearances from proposed structures to existing overhead electric infrastructure.
applicableAreas: Existing electric poles, overhead lines, and cross arms adjacent to proposed buildings
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows existing distribution poles with overhead utility lines (O.H.U.L.) along Valley View Road on the western and southern property boundaries. These poles carry cross arms (approximately 8 feet wide per standard distribution pole design) with conductors. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows building locations in relation to the property boundaries. However, no building elevation sheets are included in the site plan set, which means the poles, lines, and cross arms are not shown on any elevation view relative to the proposed buildings.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) explicitly requires that 'Building elevations shall be provided showing electric poles, overhead lines, conductors, cross arms, and property boundaries.' This is a mandatory documentation requirement when overhead electric facilities are present on or adjacent to the site. The applicant has failed to provide this required documentation. Without elevations, the three-dimensional clearance relationship between the existing poles/conductors and proposed buildings cannot be verified.

findings.comment: Electric poles, overhead lines, conductors, cross arms, and property boundaries not shown on building elevation sheets. Provide building elevations showing all overhead electric facilities with conductors, poles (with dimensions for cross arms approximately 8 feet wide), and property boundaries per UCM § 1.16.0(2).
applicableAreas: Overhead electric facilities shown on boundaries
Proposed buildings relative to OHE facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows overhead electric facilities (OHE) marked with dashed lines labeled '- OHE -' along the western and southern property boundaries. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) also confirms the OHE line along the southern boundary. However, NO BUILDING ELEVATION SHEETS are included in the site plan submittal. Elevation sheets are required to show electric poles, overhead lines, conductors, cross arms, and property boundaries in relation to the proposed buildings. The plan views show the overhead facilities and buildings but cannot adequately depict the pole positions, conductor heights, cross arm widths, or vertical clearances to buildings.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) explicitly requires building elevation sheets to show 'electric poles, overhead lines, conductors, cross arms, and property boundaries.' Plan view representation is insufficient. Building elevations provide the engineer and reviewer with the necessary three-dimensional perspective to understand conductor positions, pole heights, cross arm configurations (approximately 8 feet wide per the grouping regulatory overview), and vertical clearances to building surfaces. Without elevation sheets, the required documentation is missing and clearance compliance cannot be verified.
